title: Neratinib · extended adjuvant treatment
context_label: Hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer after adjuvant trastuzumab
schedule_summary: Neratinib is taken once daily with food for one year. The usual starting dose is 240 mg; the team may interrupt or reduce it for toxicity. Treatment starts less than one year after completing adjuvant trastuzumab.
purpose: Reduce recurrence risk as part of the agreed early-breast treatment plan.
indication_text: Hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer after adjuvant trastuzumab
administration_text: Take tablets whole with food, preferably in the morning. Do not crush or dissolve them. Do not replace a missed dose. Start the prescribed loperamide prevention plan with the first neratinib dose.
monitoring_summary: FBC monthly for the first six months, then every three months. Liver tests at week 1, monthly for the first three months, then every six weeks; test earlier for liver symptoms or significant diarrhoea. Confirm normal baseline LVEF eligibility; cardiac/LVEF assessment is clinically indicated. Review bowel symptoms, hydration, weight and interacting medicines. Continue any follow-up already required after prior trastuzumab; neratinib does not reset that plan.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Neratinib
agents.mechanism: Blocks growth signalling inside HER2-positive cancer cells
agents.explanation: Neratinib binds irreversibly to signalling enzymes in the HER family, including HER2. It is used after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy in a specific hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early-breast setting. Its effects on the bowel make early diarrhoea prevention important.
agents.watch: Start the prescribed diarrhoea-prevention plan with the first dose. Report diarrhoea early, especially poor intake, dizziness or reduced urine.

sections.title: Before the first tablet
sections.text: Confirm the one-year plan, loperamide prescription, blood-test appointments and interaction review.

sections.title: Daily treatment at home
sections.text: Take with food, preferably at the same morning time. No infusion port or pump is required for neratinib itself.

sections.title: Acid-suppression timing
sections.text: Avoid PPIs. If needed, the pharmacist specifies H2-blocker or antacid timing and checks interactions.

sections.title: After the planned year
sections.text: Confirm the stop date; endocrine therapy and early-breast surveillance may continue on their own schedules.

support.title: Diarrhoea prevention
support.text: Have the prescribed loperamide plan ready before the first tablet. Call early if diarrhoea starts or worsens.

support.title: Hydration
support.text: Follow the fluid plan and report dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.

support.title: Liver checks
support.text: Keep the week-1 and subsequent liver tests; report yellow skin, dark urine or severe nausea.

support.title: Other medicines
support.text: Check acid-suppressing medicines and all new prescriptions with the pharmacist.

items.title: Your treatment setting
items.text: Hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer after adjuvant trastuzumab

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Neratinib is taken once daily with food for one year. The usual starting dose is 240 mg; the team may interrupt or reduce it for toxicity. Treatment starts less than one year after completing adjuvant trastuzumab.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and reviews the results before treatment decisions.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: FBC monthly for the first six months, then every three months. Liver tests at week 1, monthly for the first three months, then every six weeks; test earlier for liver symptoms or significant diarrhoea.

items.title: Other treatment-specific checks
items.text: Confirm normal baseline LVEF eligibility; cardiac/LVEF assessment is clinically indicated. Review bowel symptoms, hydration, weight and interacting medicines. Continue any follow-up already required after prior trastuzumab; neratinib does not reset that plan.

items.title: Cancer review and follow-up
items.text: After early-breast treatment, breast imaging and clinical review follow the agreed plan. Routine CT/PET scans or blood tumour markers are not used to search for distant recurrence in someone without symptoms or clinical concerns.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health assessment follows endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression, menopause and other fracture risks. It has its own monitoring plan.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Agree surgery, radiotherapy and endocrine treatment as applicable; their schedules and checks remain separate.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: Do not replace a missed dose. Contact the team about diarrhoea or a treatment hold; restart and dose reductions require their instructions.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Avoid grapefruit, pomegranate and proton-pump inhibitors. If an H2 blocker is prescribed, take neratinib at least two hours before or ten hours after it; separate antacids by at least three hours. Check CYP3A/P-glycoprotein interactions with the pharmacist.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.
